_meta._note: Chapter 32 final test (ch32-test, new). Twelve multiple-choice questions on the proposal's six two-question strands: مَتَى / إِذَا (q01–02), the event (q03–04), a stated response and an event-only excerpt (q05–06), 94:7's command and meaning (q07–08, recognition only — no imperative formation), fresh authored sentences with the verb meaning supplied (q09–10), 84:1 retrieval and a fresh event-only clause (q11–12). Pass mark 80 %: 9/12 fails, 10/12 passes. Rebuilt 2026-10-02 in the proposal harvest, batch 2 (Docs/proposals/proposal-harvest-tracker.md), from Docs/proposals/chapter-32-content-proposal.md and its review amendments: the chapter now teaches what its map promised — reading an إِذَا clause. مَتَى (Chapter 31) asks; إِذَا introduces an event; the event and its response (جَوَابُ الشَّرْطِ, named only); the two فَ of 94:7 (the first continues, the second marks the response; the command is انْصَبْ, glossed — commands are Chapter 51); transfer to 84:1 and 81:1, whose ayah states no response. Al-Falaq's إِذَا وَقَبَ / إِذَا حَسَدَ are Chapter 19 retrieval; An-Nasr is left to Chapter 33. No إِنْ or jussive (Chapter 68); no tense rule is taught. Removed: the sentence-type / إِنَّ / لَيْسَ re-run of Chapter 29, لَيْسَ with a nominative predicate, إِذَا labelled حرف جر, 'a future event in the past', فَ called an imperative particle, the duplicated An-Nasr parse items, and corrupted strings.
